paragraphs: Rabbi Yose ben Pazi: Zohar, Lekh Lekha, After These Things, at the locator עשמ״ב; Sulzbach edition, at ד״ס ע״ד. When Rabbi Abba came from there, he would proclaim: ‘Who desires wealth, and who desires length of days in the world to come? Let him come and engage in Torah.’ Everyone would gather. A young unmarried man lived in his neighborhood. One day he came and said: ‘Master, I wish to occupy myself with Torah so that I shall have wealth.’ He replied: ‘Certainly.’ He asked: ‘What is your name?’ He replied: ‘Yose.’ He told his students to teach him, and they called him Rabbi Yose, master of wealth and honor. He sat and engaged in Torah. After some days he stood before him and said: ‘Master, where is the wealth?’ He said: ‘We may infer that he is not acting for Heaven’s sake.’ He entered a room and heard a voice: ‘Do not punish him. Return to him, for he will become a great man.’ He returned and told him: ‘Sit, and I shall give you wealth.’ Meanwhile a man came with a vessel of fine gold in his hand. He took it out, and light fell in the house. He said: ‘Master, I wish to merit Torah, but I have not merited it. I want someone to engage in Torah on my account, for I have much wealth left me by my father,’ and so forth, ‘and I wish to merit Torah; I shall give wealth.’ He told the young man: ‘You shall engage in Torah, and he shall give you wealth.’ He gave that cup. Rabbi Abba applied to him: ‘Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can a vessel of fine gold be its exchange.’ He toiled in Torah, and that man gave him wealth. After some days the love of Torah entered his inward parts. One day he sat weeping. His teacher found him and asked: ‘Why do you weep?’ He replied: ‘And am I giving up life in the world to come for this?’ The source reads מנחנא, alternatively אנחנא. ‘I desire only to merit for myself.’ He said: ‘Now we may infer that he acts for Heaven’s sake.’ He called that man and told him: ‘Take your wealth and give it to orphans and the poor, and I shall give you a greater portion in Torah in everything we labor over.’ Rabbi Yose returned that cup of fine gold to him. To this day the name has not left him; among his sons, Ben Pazi. This is Rabbi Yose ben Pazi, who, together with his sons, merited much Torah; see there. Tzror HaMor, Vayera, 20b, beginning, has this incident with Rabbi Yose coming before Rabbi Yochanan, as above. In the Jerusalem Talmud, Bammeh Tomnin, he spoke in Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s name. This requires examination: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina was Rabbi Yochanan’s student, whereas the Rabbi Abba mentioned in the Zohar preceded him by much. Perhaps it is the earlier Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, who was a tanna. Or it is as I wrote in the principles: later authorities wrote many matters; see Rabbi Elazar HaKappar. He related the birth of Ahavah, Rav Adda’s father; see his entry.
